subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Heat Shields: Surviving Reentry
description: Learn Heat Shields: Surviving Reentry in one minute.

hook.text: A spacecraft reentering Earth's atmosphere reaches temperatures of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Without a heat shield, it vaporizes.

buildup.text: Early capsules used ablative shields — materials that char and flake off, carrying heat away with each layer removed.

discovery.text: The Space Shuttle used ceramic tiles. Each of 24,000 tiles was uniquely shaped and had to be hand-fitted to the orbiter.

twist.text: A blunt shape creates a strong shock wave that deflects most heat away from the surface. Pointy shapes actually heat up more.

climax.text: SpaceX's Starship uses stainless steel with active cooling. Steel tolerates heat better than the carbon fiber it replaced.

punchline.text: Flat is better than pointy. Ablation beats insulation. Counterintuitive saves lives.

quiz.question: Why do blunt-shaped reentry vehicles survive better than pointy ones?
options: Blunt shapes are lighter and can carry thicker heat shield material
A blunt shape creates a strong shock wave that deflects most heat away from the surface
Pointy shapes spin uncontrollably during reentry due to aerodynamic forces
